authority: R-167 v1.5 is an additive T0 fixed-beta Hamiltonian-to-OS topology theorem and route split, not a new result number. Along the already registered EXP-000781 plus/minus tangent nets, bounded KMS tube convergence and fixed physical-time bandlimiting give convergence of every finite word Gram block to the canonical EXP-000800 mixture reconstruction. Explicit finite-block polar transports then give pointed finite-core Fell/GNS convergence on a preregistered bandlimited word list. An exact character carre-du-champ identity and Fejer Liouville filtering remove the bandlimit uniformly in cyclic two-sided L2 for each raw rational configuration character. This identifies the fixed-beta selected tangent-net Hamiltonian correlation system with the v1.4 OS envelope on every finite bandlimited word block. It is not a common-Hilbert operator strong-star limit or an all-exhaustion quasi-local limit in the locally normal mixture representation. It is not a beta-independent C-star dynamics. Exact counterexamples reject a naive label-preserving GNS embedding, inference of canonical momentum from configuration cylinders, raw characters as a bounded generator core, an asymmetric zero-source periodic mixture limit, and automatic cross-beta gluing.

registered_tangent_net.input: Fix beta>0. Use the exact EXP-000781 finite periodic Gibbs/path tangent subsequences (Lambda_n,+h_n) and (Lambda_n,-h_n), with h_n decreasing to zero, whose local cylinder laws converge to mu_+ and mu_-. Fix 0<lambda_+,lambda_-<1 and form the finite direct-sum mixture word system with weights lambda_+,lambda_-.
registered_tangent_net.limit: The mixed Euclidean cylinder kernels converge on the preregistered countable rational cylinder core to mu_0=lambda_+mu_++lambda_-mu_-. The limiting periodic reconstruction is the canonical EXP-000800 mixture system.
registered_tangent_net.scope: The net is the selected phase-tangent diagonal net. It is not the zero-source periodic sequence and it does not assert independence of all shapes, boundaries, tangent subsequences or phase pairs.

bandlimited_kms_kernel_theorem.normal_family: For each finite word of bounded configuration characters, the finite-volume KMS function is uniformly bounded on its thermal tube by the product of operator norms. Euclidean cylinder convergence on the ordered imaginary-time region and analytic uniqueness give local-uniform convergence in the tube interior.
bandlimited_kms_kernel_theorem.boundary_smoothing: The uniformly bounded analytic functions have unique weak-star boundary distributions. Convolution in every physical-time variable with a fixed L1 kernel gives locally uniform convergence of the real-time boundary functions; uniformity on compact translation sets follows from L1 translation continuity of the fixed kernel. Choosing even Fejer kernels with compact Fourier support produces a countable word list closed under star, products and rational shifts; its complex span is used.
bandlimited_kms_kernel_theorem.gram_convergence: Every fixed finite Gram matrix of the bandlimited word list converges entrywise to the corresponding EXP-000800 mixture Gram matrix.
bandlimited_kms_kernel_theorem.scope: This is convergence of selected tangent-net word kernels. It does not by itself put the raw finite-volume operators into the locally normal mixture GNS representation.

finite_block_polar_transport.construction: Enumerate a countable bandlimited word list and discard each label that is dependent in the limiting Gram form. For a retained k-block, let G_0^(k)>0 and G_n^(k) be the limit and finite Gram matrices. For large n define M_(n,k)=G_0^(-1/2)G_n^(1/2). Then M_(n,k)^*G_0M_(n,k)=G_n and M_(n,k) tends to I.
finite_block_polar_transport.operator_transport: Choose k(n) increasing diagonally and include every required product, adjoint and rational translate before testing a fixed finite set. The exact block isometries give finite-word approximate intertwining and pointed finite-core Fell/GNS convergence of each such family. No globally compatible common-Hilbert extension is inferred.
finite_block_polar_transport.scope: The transport is asymptotically canonical only after freezing the enumeration, dependence-removal rule and principal square roots. Singular limit directions are discarded through retained independent pivots rather than embedded into a lower-rank support. This is a pointed finite-core GNS/Fell identification, not a label-preserving injective embedding of the complete finite GNS spaces, a common-representation strong-star theorem or the canonical inductive local-algebra embedding.

character_dirichlet_and_filter_theorem.character: For W_xi=exp(i sum xi.q), any exact finite-volume H=p^2/(2chi)+V(q) with arbitrary q-only source, boundary and potential obeys [W_xi^*,[H,W_xi]]=(hbar^2/chi)||xi||_2^2 I and delta W_xi=i W_xi[(xi.p)/chi+hbar||xi||_2^2/(2chi)].
character_dirichlet_and_filter_theorem.duhamel: For rho=Z^(-1)exp(-beta H), delta=(i/hbar)[H,.] and the normalized Duhamel form, ||delta W_xi||_D^2=||xi||_2^2/(beta chi), exactly and uniformly in volume, source and q-only boundary terms.
character_dirichlet_and_filter_theorem.general_wstar_bridge: In a faithful normal W-star standard form, the logarithmic-mean functional calculus gives the averaged two-sided norm inequality ||X||_#^2<=||X||_D^2+(1/2)||X||_D||[log Delta,X]||_D. For a beta-KMS dynamics this is the general modular counterpart of the finite type-I R-167 v1.2 lemma. With the unaveraged v1.4 sum convention the right side is multiplied by two.
character_dirichlet_and_filter_theorem.fejer_filter: Let g_R(omega)=(1-|omega|/R)_+ and W_xi^(R)=int f_R(t)alpha_t(W_xi)dt. With a_xi=||xi||/sqrt(beta chi), Y_R=W_xi-W_xi^(R) obeys ||Y_R||_D<=a_xi/R, ||delta Y_R||_D<=a_xi and, in the unaveraged cyclic two-sided convention, ||Y_R||_#<=a_xi sqrt(2/R^2+beta hbar/R). Thus each raw character is recovered uniformly as a cyclic two-sided L2 vector after fixed-band convergence. This does not give arbitrary bandlimited left/right-context multiplier control or raw-core operator strong-star convergence. EXP-000781 local p^2 control also yields an optional O(1/R) cyclic rate.
character_dirichlet_and_filter_theorem.finite_span: For A=sum_j c_jW_(xi_j), ||delta A||_D is at most (sum_j |c_j|||xi_j||)/sqrt(beta chi).
character_dirichlet_and_filter_theorem.scope: The equality is finite-volume and form-core exact. In the limit, the uniform limsup filter bound is sufficient; equality of the limiting Dirichlet form requires a separate closure statement.

generator_and_first_tail.smooth_core: Raw W_xi is not in the bounded W-star generator domain. The bounded temporal smears A_f=int f(t)alpha_t(A)dt form a strong-star dense smooth core and obey delta(A_f)=-A_(f').
generator_and_first_tail.formal_local_jets: On the finite-support polynomial CCR core, delta_h=delta_0+hD with D(q_x)=0 and D(p_x)=u. Every fixed iterate delta_h^m(W_xi) is a finite-neighborhood polynomial times W_xi and is volume-independent once that neighborhood lies inside Lambda. In particular delta_hW_xi=delta_0W_xi and delta_h^2W_xi-delta_0^2W_xi=i h(sum_x xi_x.u)W_xi/chi.
generator_and_first_tail.coordinate_tail_rung: If H=K+W_L with W_L a q-multiplication coordinate tail, then delta_HW_xi=delta_KW_xi and (delta_H^2-delta_K^2)W_xi=-(i/chi)W_xi xi.grad W_L. Its H-Duhamel norm is at most ||xi||phi_H(|grad W_L|^2)^(1/2)/chi, hence the first acceleration tail is super-Gaussian under the registered coordinate-tail estimate.
generator_and_first_tail.scope: The smooth generator is intrinsic to the fixed-beta limit group. The formal polynomial jets and first tail rung do not sum the real-time series, prove a canonical momentum embedding, or close connected projected-tail resummation.

embedding_and_generator_no_gos.rotating_null_form: On C^2, q_n(x)=|<v_n,x>|^2 with v_n tending to e_1 has Gram forms converging to q_0(x)=|x_1|^2, but N_n is not contained in N_0. Therefore [F]_n maps to [F]_0 is not well-defined despite pointwise Gram convergence. A separate faithful-to-nonfaithful C^2 state sequence also shows GNS dimension can collapse, so no label-preserving injective embedding follows.
embedding_and_generator_no_gos.momentum_gauge: For H=p^2/(2chi)+V(q), U_a=exp(i a.q/hbar) and H_a=U_aHU_a^*=(p-a)^2/(2chi)+V(q), every bounded Euclidean q-cylinder trace is identical for H and H_a, while delta_H(q)=p/chi and delta_(H_a)(q)=(p-a)/chi. Configuration OS data alone cannot select canonical momentum or the registered polynomial generator.
embedding_and_generator_no_gos.raw_character: For xi!=0, [H,W_xi]=W_xi[(hbar/chi)xi.p+hbar^2||xi||^2/(2chi)] is unbounded. Raw rational configuration characters are an L2/form seed, not a bounded W-star generator core.
embedding_and_generator_no_gos.consequence: Use explicit finite-block transports for selected tangent-net pointed convergence, and use a temporal-smear bounded core plus an independently fixed kinetic/CCR anchor for any generator theorem.

parity_and_cross_beta_no_gos.parity: Every zero-source periodic finite-volume Gibbs/path law is parity invariant. Since mu_+ and mu_- are distinct and exchanged by parity, lambda mu_++(1-lambda)mu_- is parity invariant only for lambda=1/2. Therefore an asymmetric v1.4 mixture cannot be the zero-source periodic finite-volume limit. The symmetric mixture still requires a phase-exhaustiveness or direct convergence theorem.
parity_and_cross_beta_no_gos.cross_beta_fixture: On M_2 with diagonal configuration algebra, take (beta_1,H_1)=(1,-sigma_x) and (beta_2,H_2)=(2,-2sigma_x). Each gives a faithful stochastically positive fixed-beta KMS system, but no single inner dynamics has both Gibbs states at their stated beta because -beta_j^(-1)log rho_j differs by a nonscalar operator.
parity_and_cross_beta_no_gos.consequence: Fixed-beta OS envelopes do not automatically glue. A beta-independent algebra and one common derivation must be constructed before beta-to-infinity ground-state arguments.

route_status.closed_scope: The selected EXP-000781 plus/minus tangent net is identified with the EXP-000800 fixed-beta mixture system in bounded bandlimited word-kernel and pointed finite-core Fell/GNS topology; exact Fejer estimates recover each raw rational configuration character in cyclic two-sided L2.
route_status.not_closed: No all-shape pairwise union estimate is proved in the canonical locally normal mixture representation. The periodic zero-source symmetric mixture, canonical momentum/full Weyl bridge, connected projected-tail resummation, and beta-independent C-star dynamics remain open.

status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED: FIXED-BETA SELECTED PHASE-TANGENT HAMILTONIAN KMS WORD SYSTEMS CONVERGE TO THE CANONICAL OS MIXTURE IN BANDLIMITED KERNEL AND POINTED FINITE-CORE FELL/GNS TOPOLOGY, AND EACH RAW CONFIGURATION CHARACTER IS RECOVERED IN CYCLIC TWO-SIDED L2 BY AN EXACT UNIFORM FEJER-DIRICHLET BOUND. THIS IS NOT A COMMON-HILBERT OPERATOR STRONG-STAR OR ALL-EXHAUSTION QUASI-LOCAL LIMIT, A CANONICAL MOMENTUM GENERATOR, OR A BETA-INDEPENDENT C-STAR DYNAMICS.

verification.proof_grade: ANALYTIC exact bounded-KMS-tube boundary-smoothing and finite-block Gram-transport theorem on the registered tangent nets; pointed finite-core Fell/GNS identification; exact cyclic character double-commutator, Duhamel and Fejer estimates; exact formal jet and first coordinate-tail identities; exact finite-dimensional and rank-one embedding, momentum-gauge, parity and cross-beta hostile fixtures; primary, non-importing independent and integrated verification

no_overclaim: This package proves a selected fixed-beta phase-tangent Hamiltonian-to-OS finite-word correlation/pointed finite-core Fell-GNS identification and exact cyclic character topology reductions. It does not prove a canonical label-preserving embedding of complete finite GNS spaces, globally compatible common-Hilbert operator strong-star convergence, raw-character convergence after arbitrary left/right contexts, all-exhaustion or all-boundary Cauchy in one local-algebra representation, the periodic zero-source symmetric limit, a canonical momentum/full Weyl embedding, a beta-independent common C-star alpha, algebraic ground states, a GNS or physical gap, regulator removal, a continuum, physical empty space or a below-empty sign, Pre-A selection, C6, CP1 or Sector-A closure.
